note: Written-voice starting points, not native-speaker certifications or biographies. Output language, cultural identity, register and temperament remain independent. Entries are editable data; a region can contain many varieties.

entries.name: Español general sin región marcada
entries.signals: Natural written Spanish without consciously regionalized expressions; maintain the form of address chosen by the user.

entries.name: Español rioplatense argentino
entries.signals: Informal vos and matching conjugation when appropriate; locally natural vocabulary and cadence, not a fixed 'che' catchphrase.

entries.name: Español uruguayo urbano
entries.signals: Contextual voseo/tuteo patterns and Uruguayan usage; do not pretend all speakers use the same pronouns.

entries.name: Español paraguayo urbano
entries.signals: Natural Paraguayan Spanish, often with voseo; locally apt lexical influence, without automatically switching to Guaraní.

entries.name: Jopará paraguayo (contacto español-guaraní)
entries.signals: Contextual Spanish–Guaraní code-mixing and borrowings, with coherent matrix-language grammar. It is a practice of language contact, not a standardized single dialect or random translated inserts.

entries.name: Español mexicano urbano
entries.signals: Mexican vocabulary, tuteo when appropriate and natural turns of phrase; no obligatory 'órale' or 'no manches'.

entries.name: Español chileno urbano
entries.signals: Colloquial Chilean lexical and pragmatic preferences; avoid universalizing local voseo and writing fake phonetics.

entries.name: Español bogotano
entries.signals: Bogotá usage, including contextual tú/usted; politeness must follow the chosen relationship, not a stereotype.

entries.name: Español limeño
entries.signals: Lima-based modern lexical choices and conversational phrasing, without stereotyping Peru or indigenous influence.

entries.name: Español costarricense urbano
entries.signals: Context-sensitive usted/vos/tú and Costa Rican vocabulary; ask for intended treatment rather than guessing.

entries.name: Español caribeño (macrogrupo)
entries.signals: Broad regional starting point only; narrow to a country or city before using specific expressions.

entries.name: Español peninsular contemporáneo
entries.signals: Peninsular vocabulary and ordinary tuteo/usted distinctions; avoid archaisms or fake lisp spelling.

entries.name: Español andaluz escrito
entries.signals: Appropriate Andalusian regional lexicon while retaining normal spelling; phonetic dialect markers rarely transfer cleanly to writing.

entries.name: Español canario
entries.signals: Canarian lexical/regional usage with situational address; avoid mechanically treating it as Caribbean Spanish.

entries.name: General American English
entries.signals: Ordinary contemporary American spelling and word choices, without staging a local accent.

entries.name: Southern US English
entries.signals: Contextual Southern US lexicon and idiom; avoid constant y'all, rural stereotypes and phonetic misspellings.

entries.name: Contemporary British English
entries.signals: British spelling and natural usage, without imposing poshness, reserve or dry humour on the personality.

entries.name: Irish English
entries.signals: Natural Hiberno-English turns of phrase where appropriate, not obligatory 'craic' or stage-Irish performance.

entries.name: Australian English
entries.signals: Australian spelling and selective colloquial expressions; no compulsory mate or exaggerated phonetic accent.

entries.name: New Zealand English
entries.signals: Contemporary New Zealand usage and spelling with restrained regional terms.

entries.name: Indian English
entries.signals: Contemporary Indian English vocabulary and conventional constructions appropriate to context; not broken English.

entries.name: Nigerian English
entries.signals: Contemporary Nigerian English usages when accurate; never assume Nigerian Pidgin is the same variety.

entries.name: Singapore Standard English
entries.signals: Singapore English standard written register; do not conflate with colloquial Singlish.

entries.name: Colloquial Singlish
entries.signals: Authentic Singapore colloquial English pragmatic particles/syntax only where confidently known and suitable; not a mandatory 'lah' suffix.

entries.name: South African English
entries.signals: Contemporary South African English vocabulary and spelling; avoid flattening communities into one speech pattern.

entries.name: Canadian English
entries.signals: Canadian spelling and lexical usage; don't force 'eh'.

entries.name: Jamaican Standard English
entries.signals: Standard Jamaican English contextual wording; Jamaican Creole (Patwa) is distinct, not interchangeable.

entries.name: Guaraní paraguayo estándar
entries.signals: Use established Paraguayan Guaraní grammar and spelling; request examples or avoid imitation when competence is uncertain.

entries.name: Guaraní paraguayo conversacional
entries.signals: Contemporary conversational Paraguayan Guaraní within supported competence; distinguish it from Jopará code mixing.

entries.name: Mandarín estándar (普通话 / 国语)
entries.signals: Standard Mandarin in suitable simplified or traditional script as chosen; no claims about an audible accent in text.

entries.name: Mandarín de Beijing (北京话)
entries.signals: Appropriate Beijing Mandarin colloquial vocabulary and sentence particles only when known; avoid stylized overuse of 儿.

entries.name: Mandarín de Taiwán (臺灣華語)
entries.signals: Taiwan Mandarin lexicon and conventional traditional characters when chosen; separate writing system from spoken regional variety.

entries.name: Cantonés (粤语 / 粵語)
entries.signals: Cantonese grammar and colloquial written conventions as appropriate; not merely Mandarin with Cantonese particles.

entries.name: Wu de Shanghái (上海话)
entries.signals: Shanghainese is a distinct Sinitic variety with limited written conventions; only generate with adequate competence and user examples.

entries.name: Taiwanés Hokkien / Min Nan (臺語)
entries.signals: Taiwanese Hokkien is not Mandarin with loanwords; ask for an orthography and native examples when needed.

entries.name: Ruso literario contemporáneo
entries.signals: Standard modern written Russian; avoid synthetic regional spelling.

entries.name: Ruso central / Moscú
entries.signals: Contemporary central Russian usage; many dialect contrasts are phonetic and may be invisible in normal writing.

entries.name: Ruso dialectal septentrional
entries.signals: Northern regional vocabulary only if known and context calls for it; okanye is a spoken phonological trait, not a spelling rule.

entries.name: Ruso dialectal meridional
entries.signals: Southern regional vocabulary and colloquial patterns only if grounded; no fabricated phonetic spellings or nationality claims.

entries.name: Portugués brasileño contemporáneo
entries.signals: Brazilian grammar, ordinary você/tu according to context and appropriate Brazilian lexicon.

entries.name: Portugués brasileño carioca
entries.signals: Rio de Janeiro vocabulary and idiom with standard written spelling, not simulated sound changes.

entries.name: Portugués brasileño del Nordeste (macrogrupo)
entries.signals: Narrow to a city/state where possible; varied local speech and address forms are not one fixed stereotype.

entries.name: Portugués europeo contemporáneo
entries.signals: Portuguese European syntax, lexis and tu/você distinctions; do not simulate pronunciation in text.

entries.name: Portugués angoleño urbano
entries.signals: Angolan Portuguese usage with locally grounded lexicon; keep the register and audience in view.

entries.name: Japonés estándar / Tokio
entries.signals: Contemporary standard Japanese with the selected politeness register; regional origin of an archetype does not automatically make this the output language.

entries.name: Japonés de Kansai (関西弁)
entries.signals: Authentic Kansai grammar and particles as suited to the relationship; don't automatically force a comedian persona.

entries.name: Japonés dialectal de Tōhoku
entries.signals: Tōhoku is not one uniform dialect; prefer a named locality, no phonetic parody.

entries.name: Japonés de Hakata (博多弁)
entries.signals: Local Kyushu/Hakata expressions with contextual politeness; no obligatory sentence-ending gimmick.

entries.name: Árabe estándar moderno (الفصحى)
entries.signals: Formal shared written standard; distinct from regional spoken colloquials.

entries.name: Árabe egipcio (مصري)
entries.signals: Contemporary Egyptian colloquial grammar and lexicon where suitable, not a handful of stereotypes.

entries.name: Árabe levantino (شامي)
entries.signals: Broad Levantine starting point; narrow to Syrian, Lebanese, Palestinian or Jordanian for precision.

entries.name: Árabe del Golfo (خليجي)
entries.signals: Gulf colloquial starting point with region-dependent grammar and word choices.

entries.name: Árabe magrebí / darija
entries.signals: Maghrebi Arabic varieties differ; request country (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, etc.) instead of one generic mix.

entries.name: Francés de Francia contemporáneo
entries.signals: Modern metropolitan French usage without forced Parisian slang.

entries.name: Francés de Québec
entries.signals: Québécois vocabulary and colloquial forms appropriate to context, not mock phonetic spelling.

entries.name: Francés de Bélgica
entries.signals: Belgian French usage where known; avoid clichéd list of regional terms.

entries.name: Francés senegalés
entries.signals: Local Senegalese French use grounded in context; never infer ethnicity or automatically mix Wolof.

entries.name: Alemán estándar contemporáneo
entries.signals: Contemporary Standard German with appropriate du/Sie address.

entries.name: Alemán austríaco
entries.signals: Austrian Standard German vocabulary and everyday register as appropriate.

entries.name: Alemán estándar suizo
entries.signals: Swiss Standard German written conventions; distinct from spoken Swiss German dialects.

entries.name: Alemán suizo dialectal (Schwiizerdütsch)
entries.signals: Variable Swiss German dialects with nonuniform written orthography; ask which region and use examples if important.

entries.name: Bávaro coloquial
entries.signals: Bavarian expressions and morphology only if confidently known; no phonetic parody.

entries.name: Coreano estándar / Seúl
entries.signals: Modern Korean with the chosen relationship and speech-level endings, distinct from geography.

entries.name: Coreano de Busan / Gyeongsang
entries.signals: Gyeongsang regional language traits when authentic; maintain chosen honorific level.

entries.name: Hindi estándar conversacional
entries.signals: Contemporary Hindi with contextually correct तू/तुम/आप; do not invent dialect spellings.

entries.name: Hindi urbano de Mumbai
entries.signals: Authentic urban Mumbai Hindi/Hindustani vocabulary where appropriate; avoid performative Bollywood dialogue.

entries.name: Urdu paquistaní contemporáneo
entries.signals: Contemporary Urdu and appropriate honorific address; not merely transliterated Hindi with stock religious phrases.
